title: Verbal, Written & Digital Communication
summary: Learn how to choose and use verbal, written, and digital communication channels appropriately for different workplace situations.
objectives: Compare verbal, written, and digital workplace communication.
Choose an appropriate communication channel for different situations.
Create clear messages that include purpose, context, action, and timing.

vocab.def: The method used to send or receive information, such as conversation, email, messaging, phone, or a workplace system.
The person or group receiving a message.
The attitude or impression communicated through words, delivery, and context.
A written or recorded account of information, decisions, actions, or results.

sections.heading: Different channels serve different purposes
sections.body: A quick question may be best handled in conversation or messaging, while detailed instructions, approvals, or important decisions may need written documentation.

sections.heading: Match the message to the audience
sections.body: A useful workplace message considers what the receiver already knows, what they need to know, and what action they are expected to take.

sections.heading: Digital communication still requires professionalism
sections.body: Email, messaging platforms, shared documents, and workplace systems should be used with the same care as face-to-face communication.

sections.heading: Important information may need documentation
sections.body: Some decisions, changes, incidents, approvals, or handoffs should be recorded so the team can refer back to accurate information later.

practice.prompt: You need written approval for a change. Should you rely only on a casual hallway conversation?
practice.answer: No. Use the appropriate documented channel required by the workplace.

practice.prompt: A short message could easily be misunderstood. What can make it clearer?
practice.answer: Add the necessary context, state the purpose, identify the requested action, and include timing when relevant.

quiz.question: What is the best reason to choose one communication channel over another?
options: The channel fits the purpose, audience, urgency, and documentation needs
It is always the fastest channel
It is the channel you personally like most
All channels work equally well for every situation
quiz.answer: The channel fits the purpose, audience, urgency, and documentation needs

lab.objective: Convert the same workplace information into an appropriate verbal update, written message, and digital communication.

reflectionPrompt: Describe one situation where written communication would be more appropriate than a verbal conversation.

proofActivity.title: Prove: workplace communication
proofActivity.description: Use a workplace communication scenario to choose an appropriate channel, communicate the relevant facts clearly, distinguish assumptions or uncertainty, and identify an appropriate follow-up.
criteria: Selects an appropriate communication approach for the situation
Communicates relevant facts clearly and respectfully
Identifies an appropriate follow-up or confirmation step

prompts.observations: Relevant workplace facts or message requirements
prompts.uncertainty: What assumptions, missing context, or uncertainty remain?
